justification.statement: Kahn's argument: in a finite list of rows, repeatedly placing the first listed row with no unplaced predecessor places each row before every row its collateral names, and leaves unplaced exactly the rows on a cycle or held behind one
justification.text: The proof is Kahn's argument (A. B. Kahn, "Topological sorting of large networks", Communications of the ACM 5, 1962). A row is placed only when every row whose collateral names it is placed, so it comes after all of them. Placing a row removes its edges. The rows neither on a cycle nor held behind one form a finite set that holds all their predecessors and has no cycle, so while any of them is unplaced, one of them has no unplaced predecessor; hence every such row is placed. A row on a cycle, or held behind one, always keeps an unplaced predecessor, so it is never placed.

justification.text: The technical report's proposition, at the commit that last changed it: with the certified setup and frame coverage, the orientation corrections and an acyclic raw-seed collateral graph, solving every orbit before the orbits its seed's collateral moves keeps each completed orbit solved at later macro boundaries. The next raw seed fixes the completed orbits, since its collateral lies on later orbits, and every conjugate of it by a legal setup fixes them too. It holds at macro boundaries only (Net): during a macro, pieces of completed orbits can move and return.

reason.idea: Solve an orbit before the orbits its seed disturbs. Each later seed, and every setup's version of it, then leaves the finished orbits as they are at the end of each macro, although their pieces may move and come back during one.

steps.check: Orbit 30 is in orbit 26's collateral, so 30 has one predecessor, 26.
The first listed row with no unplaced predecessor is orbit 26.
Placing 26 releases 30, which is placed next: the order is [26, 30].
Every row is placed: no cycle.
